author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The Environmental Protection Agency is moving to repeal federal rules limiting greenhouse-gas emissions from coal- and natural-gas-fired power plants, the Associated Press reported Monday. The action would reverse a central part of the federal government’s recent effort to regulate climate pollution from the electricity sector.

The EPA says eliminating the rules would remove more than $300 billion in costs for the power industry and support energy reliability. The agency is also pursuing a separate step intended to prevent future administrations from regulating greenhouse-gas emissions from power plants under the same approach.

The policy shift affects a major source of U.S. electricity and is likely to draw responses from states, utilities, environmental groups and industry representatives. The AP report described the EPA’s announced actions and rationale; the legal and practical effects will depend on the final regulatory language and any ensuing court challenges.
dek: The Environmental Protection Agency says it is eliminating rules that limit greenhouse-gas emissions from coal- and natural-gas-fired power plants.
headline: EPA moves to repeal power-plant greenhouse gas limits
